_about: Bomber (design doc, Initial unit roster: air; turret guns engage on their own, the bomb drop is manual -- specials are deferred for the demo). EVERY VALUE IS A PLACEHOLDER proposed by Track S on 2026-10-09; the unit design sheet and its variant boards replace them. Plausible for a WWII twin-engine medium bomber (B-25, He 111 class) at true scale. Not in the demo, which flies fighters. Record shape: data/units/_schema.json.
name: Bomber

size_m._reason: medium bomber span: B-25 20.6 m, He 111 22.6 m

actions_per_turn._reason: slowest and least agile aircraft: the fewest decision points; 3 steps of 1.67 s in a 5 s turn

health._reason: built to take hits: the most pips of the three aircraft

sight_range_m._reason: slower, so it needs less look-ahead; unused until Track F's vision rule

speed_cruise_mps._reason: about 305 km/h, a medium bomber's cruise

dive_speed_max_mps._reason: not built to dive: a little past top speed

accel_mps2._reason: heavy: cruise to top in about 18 s (3-4 turns)

decel_mps2._reason: heavy and slippery: slow to shed speed

turn_rate_curve_dps._reason: half the light fighter's rate: a 36 s circle at cruise

turn_bleed_mps2._reason: twice its 2 m/s^2 of thrust: a bomber that turns hard slows down

turn_bleed_exponent._reason: induced drag grows with the square of the load factor

start_band._reason: a bomber holds height over defended targets

bands_per_step._reason: one band per step keeps a climb a deliberate, visible choice

climb_speed_cost_mps._reason: the most mass to lift; a climb from near stall is refused

dive_speed_gain_mps._reason: less than the climb costs, so a climb-and-dive loses energy overall
